methodological_rigor.justification: AI prognostic model (PRISM) trained on 15 million histological patches from 2957 Alliance cohort patients, a well-characterized randomized phase III trial (CALGB 89803). Rigorous quality control: >98% cases have single WSI, exclusions for tissue quality (n=211), blinded pathologist review. Stratified data splitting by demographic/clinical subgroups addresses confounding. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards model used appropriately for OS prediction. Internal validation on held-out cohort. Study limitations: single-institution scanning, potential overfitting despite stratified approach.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: AI-driven prognostic model demonstrating superior performance (AUC 0.70, accuracy 68.37%) over existing CRC models (15% improvement over CRC-specific methods) and foundation models (23% accuracy improvement) for stage III CRC five-year OS prediction. Validated in treatment subgroups (5FU/LV vs CPT-11), with minimal accuracy variation (1.44%). Direct clinical relevance for risk stratification and personalized therapy selection, though requires prospective validation before clinical implementation.

reporting_quality.justification: Follows TRIPOD reporting guidelines for AI prognostic models with comprehensive methodology, appropriate statistical analyses, and limitations acknowledgment. WSI dataset, model specifications, and performance metrics clearly described. However, no statement of code or model availability for external validation; Alliance cohort data access restricted. Supplementary materials referenced but limited detail on hyperparameters and training specifics.

novelty_literature.justification: PRISM represents novel integration of morphology-informed domain-specific features with foundation model embeddings for CRC prognostication. Advances beyond discrete morphological detection by capturing continuous phenotypic variability within histological patterns (tumor budding, necrosis, stroma composition). First to rigorously address limitation of K-fold validation through stratified clinical confounding mitigation. Notably superior to prior CRC models (QuantCRC, Kather et al.) by incorporating spectrum of morphological heterogeneity.

writing_presentation.justification: Comprehensive manuscript with well-organized sections on dataset, preprocessing, methodology, and results. Figure 1 effectively illustrates PRISM architecture integrating domain-specific and generic features. Limitations section thoroughly addresses single-institution scanning, potential overfitting risks, and prospective validation needs. Technical content presented accessibly. Minor: dense methods section could benefit from algorithmic pseudocode.

key_strengths: Novel AI architecture integrating morphology-informed features with foundation models, capturing continuous phenotypic variability within histological patterns
Trained on large, well-characterized cohort (2957 patients, 15M histological patches) from randomized phase III trial; rigorous quality control with blinded pathologist review
Superior prognostic performance: AUC 0.70, accuracy 68.37%, substantially outperforming CRC-specific and general-purpose models
Robust performance across clinically relevant subgroups (sex-agnostic, stable across treatment regimens) with minimal accuracy variation; demonstrates generalization beyond training confounders
Comprehensive stratified validation approach addressing critical limitation of conventional K-fold cross-validation for OS prediction
key_concerns: Single-institution WSI scanning (Ohio State) may introduce systematic bias; generalizability to different scanning platforms/stain protocols unaddressed
Internal validation only; lacks external validation cohort from independent institutions to confirm generalization
Model code and weights not available; reproducibility and independent validation limited; AI model is treated as black box with limited mechanistic interpretation
Alliance cohort heavily enrolled from cooperative group centers; applicability to general community oncology practice populations uncertain
Stage III CRC-specific; unclear if model extends to other stages or cancer types despite claims of future broader application
chief_reviewer.rationale: High-quality AI-driven prognostic study demonstrating novel morphology-aware approach with superior performance and rigorous validation strategy. Appropriate for Tier 2 journals emphasizing computational oncology advances; recommend external validation and code availability before clinical deployment.
